style.visual_style: ink-sketch: black ink on warm white paper, single stroke weight, live hand-drawn boil

characters.role: lead — the only character; stands in for the viewer
characters.body_type: six-part hand-drawn stick figure: circular head, spine, two arms, two legs. Head radius 44, stroke width 7, drawn at ~440 units tall.
characters.silhouette_notes: Readable at phone size from the silhouette alone, which is the whole reason the design is this bare. Two white-dot eyes on the head and nothing else — no mouth, no clothes, no hair. The one variable in the silhouette is whether a hand is holding the orange errand or is empty, and that difference has to carry the entire middle of the video, so it is never obscured by a limb.
props: orange errand (a small round parcel, held in the raised hand)
constraints: Motion is never hand-authored. Every action maps to a named clip in ink-theater/mocap/catalog.json.
No clip is used twice in a row.
The figure is horizontally fixed at cx; travel is expressed by sliding the world past it.
Emotion is carried by staging — empty hands, stillness, the balloon — not by facial expression, because there is no face to change.
Never cute. It does not mug, wink or address the camera.

metadata.brief: One hand-drawn ink figure on white paper, running an errand it will lose to a doorway. Deadpan and never cute; the comedy is that it keeps doing a reasonable thing. Motion comes entirely from retargeted CMU motion capture through ink-theater/ink-puppet.js — no pose is hand-authored, which is why the required_actions below are named mocap clips rather than drawn poses.

findings.note: One character. Required actions are named mocap clips rather than drawn poses, because the style forbids hand-authored character motion.
Silhouette carries the whole story: the only variable is whether the raised hand holds the errand.
